verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the sensor-board mounting orientation, top-edge connector placement, and mechanical alignment needed for short interboard cables.
The client adds a concrete PCB-layout constraint minimizing components on the inaccessible downward-facing side.

The client changes concrete prototype layout constraints by allowing flexible board dimensions, locating the sensor board on the left, permitting small side connectors, and preserving top cable access.
The client requests a concrete sensor-board placement change that moves the problematic bottom items upward and reorients them top-down.
This is the first target-specific implementation claim that all sensor-board components were successfully placed in the layout; it does not independently verify physical fit.
The single-board architecture eliminates the entire separate sensor-board layout Requirement; REMOVE is more accurate than retaining a status attribute and moving its scope to the integrated board.
